crime: In the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} starts letter after letter to her father, and every one she unwrites back to blank paper, as if she had never begun. Every morning it snows, the same prisoner stands at the courtyard fountain with crusts for the birds and calls her out to join her. She never comes out. Then, one dawn after a snowfall, she sweeps a path through the courtyard out to the girl for the first time. Her father used to sweep a path to her door like that, but only on the mornings he came home. At the fountain, the girl tips the crusts into her hands. "You feed them from tomorrow." As the girl turns to go, {WITCH_NAME} slams the girl's head against the fountain and holds her face in the snow until she is still. Back in the doorway, she puts the swept snow back, and it lies untouched, just as it was before she began. Later that morning, the prisoners find only the girl's own footprints in the snow and rule that she slipped by the fountain alone. Then a prisoner finds half of one of the girl's footprints: the heel is pressed clear, but the toe disappears under smooth snow. In the trial court, the prisoners see what it means: someone swept a path out to the girl, then put the swept snow back. And they know who undoes her own work that way: the one who unwrites her letters to her father.
fields.epitaph: She left the snow unbroken; this time, she was the one who never came.
fields.epithet: Waiting in the Doorway Before Unbroken Snow
execution: She is strapped on her back at the end of an iron trough heaped with snow. An iron broom sweeps a path down the trough toward her and stops a step short. The swept snow slides back over her face and packs smooth. The snow over her stirs, then goes still, smooth as if it had never been swept.

magic.name: As If Never Begun
magic.text: She can undo anything she has worked on with her own hands, back to before she began.
